_comment: Every item that can sit in a satchel slot. CLAUDE.md: data that will clearly vary per item lives here, never in gameplay code. scripts/ui and autoload contain no item literals.
_comment_scope: MEADOWS_VERTICAL_SLICE.md M8 asks for a minimal starting set. Orbs and the small potion joined it when the opening gained Grandpa's parting gifts and orbs stopped being a placeholder counter in throw_aim.gd — they are real inventory now, spent from the satchel by every throw. Tools and cooked food are still M8/M9 and deliberately absent rather than stubbed.
_comment_heal: `heal` is what one use restores on a creature, in HP. Present only on consumables that heal; tunable.
_comment_revive: D40 (OF32, owner: 'Grandpa should give you revives at the beginning too'). `revive` is the fraction of max HP a Revive restores when used on a FAINTED creature (0.5 == half, tunable) -- creature_instance.gd's revive() reads it, not heal(). As of D40, `heal` items (potions) refuse a fainted creature outright instead of un-fainting it; `revive` items are the only thing that clears `fainted` outside of rest (home_recovery.gd/creature beds, which still heal_fully() -- that is rest, not a potion, and stays untouched).
_comment_stack: `stack` is the slot cap. GAME_DESIGN.md 19: slot + stack, NO weight limit — there is no `weight` key here and there must never be one.
_comment_fiber: Spelled `fiber`, matching MEADOWS_VERTICAL_SLICE.md section M8 AND the harvest data the gathering work will port from the pre-Godot prototype (git show c45dee5^:src/data/harvest.json), which drops wood, stone, fiber, berries and flint under exactly these ids. The id is what harvesting keys off, so it had to match one of them; it now matches both.
_comment_colour: `colour` is the slot tile's tint. Placeholder standing in for an icon, and sampled so four resources are told apart at a glance on a 7-inch screen rather than by reading four short words.
_comment_tools: R2.1. `gathered_with` on a resource names the tool id that gathers it at full amount; a resource with no `gathered_with` (berries) is never tool-gated. item_db.gd's harvest_yield() reads it: the right tool gives the harvest node's full amount, no tool gives a reduced bare-handed amount (BAREHANDED_FRACTION, tunable), and owning some other tool but not the right one gives nothing. Tools themselves are `kind: tool`, `stack: 1` — owned, not consumed. `hammer` and `fishing_rod` exist as items now per this task's own brief but gate nothing yet: the workbench/repair loop (R2.2) and fishing (R7.6) are what will read them.
_comment_durability: R2.2. `durability` is the number of full-yield gathers a tool survives before it breaks (GAME_DESIGN.md 19: 'have durability', 'repair for free at appropriate station'). Tunable, same for all five for now. A broken tool (0 durability) stops counting as owned for item_db.gd's harvest_yield() gating until repaired -- inventory.gd tracks the current value per-slot, defaulting to this max when a slot carries no durability key of its own (so a freshly-added tool needs no special-cased add-time write). Only `axe`/`pickaxe`/`knife` actually lose durability today, from harvest_node.gd's gather loop; `hammer` and `fishing_rod` carry the field for GAME_DESIGN.md consistency but nothing damages them yet, matching R2.1's own precedent for those two.
_comment_satiety: D29. `satiety` is how much of player_vitals.gd's satiety meter one use restores (see data/config/vitals.json); `buff` is that same use's optional temporary buff, passed straight through to player_vitals.gd's eat() as-is: { id, stat, amount, duration_s }. Only berries carry it so far. Nothing calls eat() from an eating action yet -- that wiring lands with the HUD pass, per this task's brief.
_comment_tm: OF29 (owner: 'I can pick up a TM but it needs to go in my inventory and then I see it's stats and choose who to teach it to'). A `kind: "tm"` item is a teaching disc you carry: its id is EXACTLY the matching data/moves/tms.json id (that is the whole link between the two files -- tests/test_moves.gd asserts it both ways, so a TM item with no TM entry, or a TM entry with no item, fails the build). `move` names the data/moves/moves.json id it teaches and must match that TM entry's own `move_id`; the backpack detail view reads power/type/slot from move_db.gd and the compatibility list from tm_db.gd rather than duplicating either here. `stack: 1` because a TM is now CONSUMED on teach (owner-directed change to R4.4's never-consumed design) -- one disc teaches one creature, so a satchel slot holding 'a stack of TMs' would be a lie about what the player can actually do with it.
_comment_coin: D39 (OF31, owner: 'Make the villagers so I can trade with them'). The owner chose a simple coin currency, and `coin` is an ORDINARY item in this table for that reason -- it stacks in a satchel slot, shows in the backpack like everything else, saves through the same inventory array, and can be dropped in a death satchel. There is no wallet, no second store and no `coins` field on game_state, and there must never be one: the moment currency lives somewhere else, every screen that shows your things has to learn about it separately. `kind: currency` is descriptive only -- nothing branches on it (item_db.gd's only kind branch is `tool`), it exists so the backpack detail line can say what this is. Prices are NOT here: they are per-vendor and tunable, and live in data/config/trade.json.
_comment_icons: M-G groundwork. `icon` is a res:// path to a 64px Kenney Game Icons silhouette (see docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md's 'Item + shared UI icons' row for the per-item source mapping and its honest mismatches -- this pack has no literal axe/wood/flask glyphs, so several are the closest available stand-in, same convention as the map icons row). `description` is the fuller inventory-detail text; `blurb` stays as the shorter existing field, both kept side by side rather than one replacing the other. Joined with the UI icon-set vendoring pass in the same commit-to-be.
_comment_rootstone: SD18. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md 10: the first of the Meadows' two progression-tier materials, above baseline wood/stone/fiber/berries. `gathered_with: pickaxe` matches the existing stone convention -- Rootstone is a harder seam, not a different gathering verb. SD16 (a sibling item, quarry harvest nodes) owns where it is actually found in the world; this entry only makes it a real, nameable satchel item so SD18's recipes have something to spend. `kind: resource` (same as wood/stone/fiber) rather than a new kind -- nothing branches on kind besides `tool`, so a fourth resource-shaped id needs no new code path.
_comment_ironwood: SF31. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md §3 Band 4 and §10: the SECOND and LAST of the Meadows' two progression-tier materials, above baseline wood/stone/fiber/berries and alongside Rootstone. `gathered_with: axe` because it is wood -- the spec's own note that it 'does not need to literally be iron' cuts both ways, and giving a hardwood a new gathering verb would be a mechanic where the spec asked for a tier. `kind: resource`, same as Rootstone, so no new code path. Where it grows is `data/config/harvest.json`'s `ironwood` nodes (the old-growth stands on the Rise's south-west flank, spec Band 4's 'old-growth forest'); what it buys is `data/recipes/recipes_ironwood.json`, and that file's own header holds the rule this tier is judged by: nothing the stronghold needs may require a THIRD new material.
_comment_sigils: SF34, spec §3 Band 4. Three physical items, one per regional captain, each granted through that captain's `reward` block in data/config/trainers.json. `kind: key` and `stack: 1`, exactly like `south_bridge_key` -- they are gate items, and the gate is SB10's `item_gate.gd` requiring all three at once, not a level check and not a UI lock. There is no fourth sigil and no way to buy, craft or find one: beating the captain IS the acquisition.
_comment_saddle_frame: SD18/R6.2. An intermediate crafted component, not a gathered resource -- `kind: material` says so without inventing a branch nothing reads yet (same 'descriptive only' rule `coin`'s `kind: currency` documents). Consumed later by the Riding Saddle (R6.2, spec Band 4) once the saddle recipe itself is built; this item and the recipe that makes it are SD18's whole contribution toward that -- no riding code, no mount/dismount, nothing here reads or writes anything about a creature.

coin.name: Coin
coin.blurb: Village coin. Mira takes it, and pays it.
coin.description: Small struck coins, worn smooth at the rims from passing hand to hand around the square. Mira the merchant counts in them, and so does anyone else in the Meadows with something to sell.

wood.name: Wood
wood.blurb: Cut from the oaks. Everything early is made of it.
wood.description: Rough-cut lengths from the meadow's oaks. It is the first thing you gather and the last thing you stop needing — walls, tools and campfires all start here.

stone.name: Stone
stone.description: Hard grey chunks worked loose from an outcrop, heavier in the hand than the wood pile. Foundations and hearths want it, and a pickaxe pulls it free whole.

fiber.name: Fiber
fiber.blurb: Stripped from meadow grass. Binds and stuffs.
fiber.description: Long green strands stripped clean from meadow grass. Not much to look at alone, but bindings, stuffing and cord all lean on it.

berries.name: Berries
berries.blurb: A handful off a bush. Food buffs, never starvation.
berries.description: A cupped handful picked straight off a meadow bush, still warm from the sun. A quick bite tops up satiety and leaves a little spring in your step for a couple of minutes after.

rootstone.name: Rootstone
rootstone.blurb: A harder seam than the outcrops. Worth the extra swing.
rootstone.description: Dense, root-veined stone pulled from a deeper seam than the meadow's ordinary outcrops. The pickaxe that cracks regular stone loose bites into this too, slower and with more effort — and what it makes is worth the wait.

ironwood.name: Ironwood
ironwood.blurb: Upper-Meadows hardwood. Dulls an ordinary axe and outlasts everything you build from it.
ironwood.description: Close-grained wood cut from the old-growth stands on the Rise's flank, so dense a fresh-cut round barely floats. It is still wood — the axe is still the tool — but it takes twice the swinging, and what it braces does not give.

orb_prime.name: Prime Orb
orb_prime.blurb: Ironwood-sprung bands. The best odds the Meadows can build.
orb_prime.description: A greater orb rebuilt around a sprung ironwood core, so the bands close harder and hold longer instead of flexing open on the first surge. The last rung of the tier ladder the Meadows has materials for.

potion_large.name: Ridge Tonic
potion_large.blurb: A proper dose, brewed from ironwood bark. For the long fights.
potion_large.description: Bitter resin boiled out of ironwood bark and cut with berry pulp. More than twice a small potion's worth in one go — the thing you carry into a gauntlet where there is no time to stop and pour three.

field_sigil.name: Field Sigil
field_sigil.blurb: The Field Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
field_sigil.description: A heavy bronze disc struck with Team Tether's mark and the ploughed-furrow device of the high pasture posting. A captain carries one, and hands it over when they lose — the officers' own rule, and they keep it.

ridge_sigil.name: Ridge Sigil
ridge_sigil.blurb: The Ridge Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
ridge_sigil.description: The same bronze disc, struck instead with the wind-ridge's three-peak device and worn pale along one edge by a lanyard that has spent years in a crosswind.

river_sigil.name: River Sigil
river_sigil.blurb: The Riverwatch Captain's own. One of three that turn the Hall approach.
river_sigil.description: The Riverwatch posting's disc, its device a channel running between two banks. Water-stained, and kept polished anyway.

saddle_frame.name: Saddle Frame
saddle_frame.blurb: A rootstone-braced skeleton. Wants leather and a creature's back, in that order.
saddle_frame.description: A rigid frame built to take real weight, its joints braced with worked rootstone rather than plain wood. Not a saddle yet — just the part that has to be right before the rest of one is worth building.

orb_basic.name: Orb
orb_basic.blurb: Plain make, from Grandpa's pack. A good throw matters more than a good orb.
orb_basic.description: A plain, unmarked sphere from Grandpa's old pack — no dial, no fittings, nothing fancy. It works because your throw does the work, not the orb.

orb_greater.name: Greater Orb
orb_greater.blurb: Reinforced tether bands. Meaningfully better odds than a plain orb.
orb_greater.description: A reinforced take on the plain orb, its tether bands doubled and set tighter. A creature caught in this one has a real fight on its hands before it breaks free.

potion_small.name: Small Potion
potion_small.blurb: Patches a creature's scrapes. For your creature, mind — you get soup.
potion_small.description: A small dose that closes cuts and eases bruising on a creature fast. It only works on a creature — for you, it's soup and rest, same as always.

revive.name: Revive
revive.blurb: Brings a fainted creature back up, half strength. Nothing else does.
revive.description: A denser, costlier draught than a potion, and the only thing that raises a creature back up once it's fainted. It comes back at half its full strength — a proper rest is still what finishes the job.

axe.name: Axe
axe.blurb: Bites into oak cleanly. Bare hands barely dent it.
axe.description: A proper woodcutter's edge. It takes a full swing off an oak in the time bare hands would still be scraping bark, and it wears down a little with every tree.

pickaxe.name: Pickaxe
pickaxe.blurb: Cracks stone loose whole. Bare hands just bruise.
pickaxe.description: Heavy-headed and built for outcrops. It cracks a full block of stone loose in one go where bare hands would only bruise a knuckle against it.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.blurb: For the workbench, not the woods. Free repairs start here.
hammer.description: A workbench tool, not a woodcutting one. Bring a worn-out tool to the bench with this in hand and the repair costs nothing but time.

knife.name: Knife
knife.blurb: Strips fiber in one clean pull.
knife.description: Short, sharp, and built for stripping — one clean pull takes fiber off meadow grass that bare hands would only tear at unevenly.

fishing_rod.name: Fishing Rod
fishing_rod.blurb: For water that doesn't exist yet.
fishing_rod.description: A proper rod and line, ready the moment there's water worth casting into. For now it just rides in the satchel, waiting.

tm_stone_rush.name: TM: Stone Rush
tm_stone_rush.blurb: A teaching disc. One creature, one lesson.
tm_stone_rush.description: A flat grey disc that hums faintly when a ground-type creature is near. Hold it out and the creature takes the shape of the move straight off it — once. The disc goes dull afterwards.

tm_burrow_strike.name: TM: Burrow Strike
tm_burrow_strike.blurb: A teaching disc. One creature, one lesson.
tm_burrow_strike.description: Earth-brown and gritty to the touch, this one carries the trick of coming up underneath something instead of at it. A ground-type creature learns it in a single sitting, and the disc is spent.

castle_gate_key.name: Old Key
castle_gate_key.blurb: Heavy and old. Something nearby is still locked.
castle_gate_key.description: Iron gone dark with age, too heavy for the small lock it probably once fit. Something nearby is still shut tight, and this is the only thing you own that might open it.

rootstone.name: Rootstone
rootstone.blurb: Veined stone out of the quarry. Better than what you have.
rootstone.description: Grey stone shot through with pale veins that run like roots, prised out of the Old Quarry's floor. It takes an edge and a fitting far better than ordinary stone, which is why everything you already own can be made better with it.

south_bridge_key.name: South Bridge Key
south_bridge_key.blurb: Oskar's own. Turns the old crossing south of the village.
south_bridge_key.description: Plain iron, kept oiled and working rather than decorative -- a bridgehand's tool, not a keepsake. Oskar hands it over the moment he loses fair, square terms he was plain about from the start. It turns the mechanism at the old south bridge.

rootstone.name: Rootstone
rootstone._comment: SD17. MEADOWS_PROGRESSION_SPEC.md Sec10: the FIRST of exactly two tier materials in the whole biome (Rootstone, then Ironwood) on top of wood/stone/fiber/berries. The Burrow Warrens' deposits are its first source in the world; the Old Quarry is the other, and SD18 owns every recipe that spends it -- per that item, Rootstone only ever UPGRADES something the player already has (better orb tier, workbench, gathering tool, saddle component), never opens a new tree. The icon reuses the existing `stone` silhouette on purpose: the icon set has no rootstone glyph, this is an honest stand-in in the same convention several other items already use, and it is not new asset sourcing.
rootstone.blurb: Green-veined stone from deep ground. Better than plain rock.
rootstone.description: Grey stone shot through with living green veins that keep their colour long after the block is broken out. It comes only from deep seams -- warrens, old quarry faces -- and everything made with it comes out stronger than the same thing made of ordinary rock.

heartstone.name: Heartstone
heartstone._comment: SD17 / R4.6. The evolution catalyst the evolution gate was built for and then left switched off waiting on -- see data/config/progression.json's `_comment_evolution`, which named this exact item and this exact backlog entry a phase in advance. `evolution.mudsnout.item_id` is now `heartstone`, and the one in the world sits in the Burrow Warrens' branch chamber behind the guardian. `stack: 1` because there is exactly one, and consuming it in an evolution is what removes it from play. Same honest icon stand-in as `rootstone` above.
heartstone.blurb: Warm to hold, and beating slowly.
heartstone.description: A dark red stone the size of a fist, warm in a way stone should not be, with a slow pulse somewhere under the surface. A creature held close to one has been known to finish becoming whatever it was already turning into.

mill_bridge_gear._comment: SE27, and SB10's Gate 2 (SE22's Old Mill Crossing). Added here by SE27 because the rescue that hands it over needs a real item to hand over; SE22 is building the crossing that reads it. IF A SIBLING TASK ALSO ADDED THIS ID, THE TWO ENTRIES ARE A DUPLICATE TO RESOLVE AT MERGE -- keep one, and keep whichever `icon` path actually has a PNG behind it (this one is generated by tools/gen_item_icons.py::icon_mill_bridge_gear).
mill_bridge_gear.name: Mill Bridge Gear
mill_bridge_gear.blurb: The drive gear out of the mill crossing. Team Tether took it; you took it back.
mill_bridge_gear.description: A machined bronze cog, heavier than it looks, with a keyway cut through the bore for the shaft it seats on. Team Tether did not break the Old Mill Crossing -- they simply removed the one part that made it work, and then removed the one person who knew where it went. Refitted, the crossing works again, for good.

_comment_held: Tools carry the mesh they appear in the trainer's hand as. Owner playtest: "the tools exist but you can't pull them out when you're exploring and use them" -- before this a tool was an inventory row and nothing else, and pressing it on the hotbar only repaired it. `scripts/player/tool_hold.gd` bone-attaches `held_model` to the trainer's hand, using the same BoneAttachment3D pattern the carried torch already uses (scripts/player/torch.gd). `held_offset`/`held_rotation_deg` are the fit in that hand and are TUNABLE. An empty `held_model` means the tool is carried but never drawn -- fishing_rod, which has no water to fish yet and no vendored rod mesh (D24: no new asset families for one prop).
